subject: art-design
source_note: Topic structure follows the OCR GCSE Art & Design specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Portfolio
units.blurb: Sustained project meeting the four assessment objectives

units.name: Externally set task
units.blurb: Response to an OCR starting point with a supervised outcome

units.name: Areas of study (titles)
units.blurb: The disciplines and media learners work in

topics.name: Developing Ideas Through Investigations
topics.blurb: AO1: research sources, artists and contexts to generate ideas

topics.name: Refining Through Media & Processes
topics.blurb: AO2: experiment with media, materials, techniques and processes

topics.name: Recording Ideas & Observations
topics.blurb: AO3: record insights through drawing and other visual means

topics.name: Presenting a Personal Response
topics.blurb: AO4: realise intentions in a meaningful final outcome

topics.name: Responding to a Set Starting Point
topics.blurb: Interpret an OCR theme and generate a personal direction

topics.name: Preparatory Studies
topics.blurb: Research, experiment and develop ideas before the exam

topics.name: Supervised Final Outcome
topics.blurb: Produce a resolved outcome under supervised time

topics.name: Photography
topics.blurb: Location, studio and the moving image

topics.name: Textile Design
topics.blurb: Printed, digital, fashion and stitched textiles

topics.name: Critical & Contextual Studies
topics.blurb: Artistic movements, popular culture and natural forms

connections.why: Studying artists, movements and contexts gives learners sources to investigate
Fine-art media and processes are explored and refined in the portfolio
Graphic techniques are among the media a learner experiments with
Photography is a recording method for capturing observations and ideas
Textile materials and techniques are developed through experimentation
3D processes such as ceramics are trialled while refining the project
Initial investigations feed the experimentation that refines a response
Experiments are documented as ideas and observations are recorded
Recorded studies are pulled together into the final personal outcome
The realised outcome must connect back to the ideas first investigated
The same investigation skills are used to interpret the set starting point
Media experimentation underpins the preparatory studies for the task
Realising a personal response transfers directly to the supervised outcome
A chosen direction guides the preparatory research and experimentation
Preparatory studies are resolved into the outcome made under supervision
Contextual understanding of movements informs practical fine-art choices
